thread:
Marta L: Morning — NovaHealth onboarding failing with bursts of 429s during the automated warmup smoke run. Started after yesterday's rollout.
Ethan P: Which SDK and env?
Marta L: Go SDK v1.4.0 running in serverless containers (50 instances). Warmup fires ~200 parallel requests across instances.
Rohit K: BuildBot: deploy novahealth-staging v3.14 -> success :white_check_mark: 
Marta L: Snippet from one worker's stderr: 
```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
x-rate-limit-remaining: 0
x-request-id: nh-7a2b
{"error":"rate_limited", "reason":"concurrency"}

goroutine 52 [running]:
runtime/pprof.writeRuntimeProfile(0x7f4c0c, 0xc0000b6000)
...
```
Ethan P: Are they doing per-worker ephemeral tokens or a shared cache?
Marta L: Per-worker ephemeral session tokens, TTL=30s for the test. When TTL expires, many workers refresh at once.
Rohit K: That TTL + high instance count explains the waves. Two-pronged approach: short-term quota routing + SDK-side changes.
Rohit K: SDK config we recommended to NovaHealth (Go example):
```go
// warmup-friendly settings
client := redwood.NewClient(&redwood.Config{
  TokenCacheTTLSeconds: 45,
  MaxPreflightConcurrency: 3, // coalesce refreshes
  EnableHTTP2: true, // reuse connections
  RetryBaseMs: 300,
  RetryMaxAttempts: 5,
  JitterMs: 800,
})
```
Ethan P: Also recommend changing warmup flow: create a single long-lived warmup token (TTL 10m) used only during warmup, then rotate back to short TTL in prod. Cuts the expiry boundary wave.
Marta L: I pushed the TokenCacheTTL change + reduced parallelism in their warmup job and restarted. 429s reduced but a few persisted during the high-water mark.
Rohit K: I'll open a temporary onboarding quota route to a larger pool for 2h so they can finish smoke runs without hitting global limits.
Ops-Bot: @Rohit K increased concurrency quota for org nova-health by 30% and routed traffic to onboarding-pool for 2h (manual escalation).
CS-Bot: Account note created: temporary quota/routing applied; SDK recommendations shared; follow-up enablement session scheduled.
Marta L: Re-ran warmup with long-lived warmup token + HTTP/2 enabled. Verified 60m of stable runs, no 429s after the changes.
Ethan P: I'll draft a short KB "Connection reuse + token strategies for large warmups" with the snippets and a diagram. ETA 3h.
Marta L: Great — thanks everyone. Closing once KB links added to account notes. :thumbsup:
